# Third-party notices — Hapimatic core

The Hapimatic core is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 only (see `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`). The `hapi` executable also contains, or downloads on request, the third-party software listed below. Each component is used under its own license, reproduced here as shipped by its authors. The machine-readable software bill of materials is `sbom/hapimatic-core.cdx.json`.

This file covers the 617 npm packages in the core's runtime dependency closure (a superset of what the bundlers emit) and the non-npm components, and reproduces the notice for the happy-cli code in the `cli` package. Build tools that are not distributed are listed in the SBOM but need no notice here.

## Code derived from happy-cli

Part of the `cli` package derives from happy-cli (<https://github.com/slopus/happy-cli>), Copyright (c) 2024 Kirill Dubovitskiy, used under the MIT License. That code is compiled into the `hapi` executable. `cli/NOTICE` in the source tree, reproduced below, lists the derived files and carries the license text:

- "AGPL-3.0-only": every other file, including files written later for

  file incorporates code moved out of a happy-cli file, that code remains
  available under the MIT License above.

repository's history (renames included) also appears in the history of
slopus/happy-cli.

## Components outside npm

### bun 1.4.4 — MIT AND LGPL-2.1-only

The JavaScript runtime `bun build --compile` embeds in every hapi executable. Bun is MIT; it statically links JavaScriptCore/WebKit and tinycc (LGPL) and the permissively licensed native libraries listed below. Source: <https://bun.com>.

Bun statically links the following libraries into every executable it compiles (Bun's statement: <https://bun.com/docs/project/licensing>):

- JavaScriptCore / WebKit (oven-sh/webkit fork) — LGPL-2.0 / LGPL-2.1
- tinycc — LGPL-2.1
- boringssl — several (OpenSSL / ISC / MIT)
- brotli — MIT
- c-ares — MIT
- HdrHistogram_c — CC0-1.0 or BSD-2-Clause
- highway — Apache-2.0
- libarchive — several (mostly BSD-2-Clause)
- libbase64 — BSD-2-Clause
- libdeflate — MIT
- libicu — Unicode / ICU
- libjpeg-turbo — BSD-3-Clause / IJG / Zlib
- libspng — BSD-2-Clause (libpng portions)
- libuv (Windows builds only) — MIT
- libwebp — BSD-3-Clause
- lol-html — BSD-3-Clause
- ls-hpack — MIT (bundled xxhash: BSD-2-Clause)
- ls-qpack — MIT
- lsquic — MIT (Chromium portions: BSD-3-Clause)
- mimalloc — MIT
- picohttp — Perl License or MIT
- simdutf — Apache-2.0
- sqlite (Linux / Windows builds) — public domain
- Tigerbeetle IO code — Apache-2.0
- uSockets / uWebSockets fork — Apache-2.0
- zlib-ng — Zlib
- zstd — BSD-3-Clause or GPL-2.0

JavaScriptCore/WebKit and tinycc are licensed under the GNU Lesser General Public License. Their source code is available at <https://github.com/oven-sh/webkit> and <https://github.com/oven-sh/bun>. Because the complete source of Hapimatic and its build scripts are published under the AGPL, you may rebuild the `hapi` executable with a modified Bun (and so a modified JavaScriptCore) using `bun run build:single-exe`.

### ripgrep 14.1.1 — Unlicense OR MIT

Prebuilt `rg` binary, one archive per platform under cli/tools/archives/, embedded in the executable and unpacked at first run (the `ripgrep` RPC). Source: <https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep>.

```text
This project is dual-licensed under the Unlicense and MIT licenses.

You may use this code under the terms of either license.
```

Prebuilt `difft` binary, one archive per platform under cli/tools/archives/, embedded in the executable and unpacked at first run (the `difftastic` RPC). Source: <https://github.com/Wilfred/difftastic>.

### sherpa-onnx 1.13.8 — Apache-2.0

Speech-recognition Node addon (with the onnxruntime shared libraries, MIT), downloaded from the npm registry and sha256-verified only when a user installs the optional voice-input extension. Never bundled into the binary. Source: <https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx>.

### NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B (v2 and v3, int8) v2, v3 — CC-BY-4.0

Speech model downloaded from the sherpa-onnx releases, sha256-verified, only when a user installs the voice-input extension. The extension's UI shows the CC-BY-4.0 attribution (voice-input/artifacts.ts ENGINE_ATTRIBUTION). Source: <https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2>.

### Silero VAD silero_vad.onnx — MIT

Voice-activity-detection model downloaded with the voice-input extension, sha256-verified. Source: <https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad>.
